allowed_successor_shape.statement: Error atoms propagate as visible Error successors and are not silently converted to Empty or ordinary values.

The visible lts:he transition frontier is the implementation counterpart of OSLF ◇: zero successors for quiescent/Empty, one successor per visible nondeterministic branch, and Error propagation as an Error successor.
match emits one successor per successful active-space match and emits Empty only for the no-match branch.
unify emits the success continuation on local match and the failure continuation on local no-match.
chain emits successors obtained by substituting each evaluated input result into the continuation template.
Each equation query result becomes a successor that re-enters metta evaluation at the substituted right-hand side; no-match returns the original call unchanged.
formal HE eval of an unreduced expression surfaces the inner expression, while he-compat surfaces Rust HE 0.2.10's wrapped eval expression.
TypeCast either returns the original atom on a type match or returns Error(atom, BadType(expected, actual)) on mismatch.
A grounded/native result is treated as an opaque premise result and each returned atom re-enters metta evaluation with the caller expected type.
formal HE reports NoReturn when a function body exits without return; he-compat reproduces Rust HE 0.2.10's fresh-result surface for the compatibility lane.
superpose emits one successor per tuple element and Empty for the empty tuple.
collapse collects the terminal visible results of the nested evaluation frontier.
context-space and evalc use the active interpreter space as the successor context.

premise_flow.statement: A function call may enter the typed function path only after the function type is applicable to the actual argument list and expected return type.

After the operator is evaluated, arguments are evaluated in the order and with the expected types dictated by the selected function type; Empty/Error short-circuit rather than becoming ordinary argument values.
match first parses the active-space query, then emits one successor for each space match and Empty for no-match.
unify has exactly the local-match success branch and the local-no-match failure branch, each re-entering evaluation with the selected continuation term.
chain evaluates its input term, substitutes the result through the named variable in the continuation template, and continues from that continuation.

formal_he.doc_surface_sentence: get-doc and help! follow the documented stdlib documentation surface for the active language/profile; extension-only documented surfaces are hidden. Rust HE 0.2.10 get-doc arity failures are reproduced only by he-compat.
formal_he.eval_surface_sentence: When the eval instruction reaches a non-reducible expression E, the user-visible formal-HE result is E itself.
formal_he.scope: Spec-faithful HE interpretation used as the formal base for OSLF/NTT/DTT work. This is the default --lang he path and is also available explicitly as --profile he.

he_compat.scope: Literal compatibility catalog for upstream Hyperon Experimental HE 0.2.10. This lane intentionally reproduces observed Rust HE surface quirks; formal/spec-faithful behavior belongs to --lang he / --profile he.
